zebralogic.title: Consolidate Direct Equivalences
zebralogic.principle: When a clue directly equates two attribute values, record that equivalence immediately and propagate it to all categories; without this, you may miss fixed pairings and waste reasoning steps.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: As soon as a clue states that two values are the same (e.g., "X is Y"), create a direct mapping and use it in subsequent deductions.
zebralogic.example: Failing to note that "the person who enjoys knitting is the person who owns a Toyota Camry" leads to duplicate work and missed constraints.

zebralogic.title: Assign Fixed Positions Immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue pins an attribute to a specific house number, assign it right away and propagate constraints; without this, you may waste time exploring impossible placements.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a house number (e.g., "the Ford F150 is in house 2"), record that placement immediately.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring that the Ford F150 is in house 2 can later cause contradictory assignments.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Adjacency for 'next to' and Ordered Left
zebralogic.principle: Adjacency clues ('next to', 'directly left of', 'directly right of') require the two referenced houses to be immediate neighbors; without this, you may place them too far apart.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue uses adjacency language, enforce a distance of exactly one house between the two items.
zebralogic.example: Treating "next to" as merely "somewhere left of" places items incorrectly and breaks other constraints.

zebralogic.title: Output Solution in Expected JSON Table Format
zebralogic.principle: The verifier expects a JSON object with a "header" array and a "rows" array; any deviation in structure or missing fields causes rejection.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After completing reasoning, output the final answer exactly as a JSON object with the required keys and no extra surrounding text.
zebralogic.example: Providing the solution as plain text or with extra commentary leads to parsing failure.

zebralogic.title: Keep Reasoning Concise to Avoid Token Truncation
zebralogic.principle: Reasoning must be short enough that the final JSON fits within the model's output limit; overly long explanations cause the answer to be cut off.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During reasoning, keep each step brief, avoid restating full clues, and stop once the deduction is clear.
zebralogic.example: Repeating every clue verbatim leads to token overflow and a missing final answer.

zebralogic.title: Preserve Original Attribute Tokens (Case and Spelling)
zebralogic.principle: Attribute values must be reproduced exactly as given, including case, spaces, and punctuation; otherwise the verifier will treat them as mismatches.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing the final JSON, copy attribute strings verbatim from the problem statement.
zebralogic.example: Writing "Tesla Model 3" instead of "tesla model 3" causes a mismatch.

zebralogic.title: Interpret Directional Ordering Correctly
zebralogic.principle: Clues with "somewhere to the right of" or "somewhere to the left of" enforce a strict ordering but not adjacency; misreading them as adjacent leads to wrong placements.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions "somewhere to the right/left", enforce only the ordering relation, not immediate neighbor constraints.
zebralogic.example: Treating "somewhere to the right of" as "directly right of" can violate other constraints.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Exclusion Constraints for Specific House Numbers
zebralogic.principle: If a clue forbids an attribute from a particular house, record that exclusion immediately; without this, you may assign a value to a prohibited house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue says "X is not in house N", mark house N as unavailable for X.
zebralogic.example: Assigning Arnold to house 4 despite "Arnold is not in the fourth house" leads to contradiction.

zebralogic.title: Transitive Ordering Inference
zebralogic.principle: When multiple ordering clues form a chain, combine them to infer indirect orderings; without this, you may miss necessary position constraints.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After collecting all ordering clues, compute the transitive closure to deduce implied orderings before placing items.
zebralogic.example: From "Arnold > BMW", "Victorian > Eric" and "Bob > Victorian", deducing "Bob > Eric" helps narrow placements.

zebralogic.title: Summarize Clues Concisely
zebralogic.principle: Rewrite each clue as a short symbolic relation (e.g., "Arnold > BMW", "Mediterranean = cooking") instead of restating the full sentence; without this, the reasoning can become too verbose and exceed token limits.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Immediately after reading the clue list, before detailed deduction, convert each clue to a concise shorthand.
zebralogic.example: Repeating the full natural‑language clue "The person who enjoys knitting is the person who owns a Toyota Camry" verbatim inflates token count and may cause truncation.

zebralogic.description: Generating overly long reasoning before the final answer, causing token truncation.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model tries to be thorough and repeats full clue text, exceeding the token budget.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning brief, summarize clues, and place the final JSON at the end of the response.

zebralogic.description: Providing the solution in a format not recognized by the verifier.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model outputs the answer as plain text or with extra formatting, not as the required JSON object.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Follow the exact JSON schema with "header" and "rows" keys and no extra surrounding text.

zebralogic.description: Using incorrect case or synonyms for attribute values.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model normalizes text or guesses alternative phrasing, altering the required tokens.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute strings verbatim from the problem statement.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses "left of" with "right of" or treats them as symmetric.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Explicitly map "left" to lower house numbers and "right" to higher numbers.

zebralogic.description: Treating adjacency clues as non‑adjacent ordering, leading to placement errors.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model interprets "next to" as just "somewhere left/right" rather than immediate neighbor.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Enforce a distance of exactly one house for adjacency clues.
